ann_36.original: The direct edges form a linear risk score that carries most of the model's ranking: replacing the whole part by its training mean lowers the training AUC from 0.947 to 0.811. The number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy dominates it, at 2.61 per sd through its own edge (removing that edge alone lowers the AUC to 0.907). Self-probe on the typical case: predicted risk climbs from 12% with no coloured vessels to 71% with one and 98% with two. Female sex lowers the score directly (-1.57 per sd on the female indicator, and 0.39 per sd on the male indicator, which pushes the same way because that indicator is the complement of the female one). A flat ST segment raises it (0.74 per sd) and an upsloping one lowers it (-0.83 per sd); typical angina (-0.78) and non-anginal pain (-0.74 directly, besides its role in the heart-rate gate) lower it relative to the other chest-pain types. Cholesterol raises it (0.87 per sd) and maximum heart rate lowers it (-0.47 per sd directly, besides the heart-rate gate). Normal fasting blood sugar raises the score through its direct edge (0.63 per sd), the opposite of its role inside the ST-depression gate. The remaining edges are listed in the attached formula. This part is a weighted sum; its reading in domain terms is the list of signs above, so beyond the vessel-count self-probe it is described rather than explained.

ann_37.original: The predicted risk is the sigmoid of a sum on the logit scale: the direct linear score, plus the three gates each weighted by its output edge, plus the output bias (formula attached). Two gates raise risk (ST depression; exercise angina in women) and one lowers it (high maximum heart rate). By ablation the direct terms matter most (training AUC 0.947 falls to 0.811 without them), then the ST-depression gate (0.938), the sex and angina gate (0.941) and the heart-rate gate (0.945). Self-probe of the additive combination, on a constructed woman with exercise angina, 2 mm of ST depression, non-anginal pain and a maximum heart rate of 170 bpm: the direct score contributes -8.12, the ST-depression gate 0.62, the sex and angina gate 2.08 and the heart-rate gate -1.26, giving a score of -7.37 and a predicted risk of 0.1%: the gates partly cancel and the direct score, driven by female sex and non-anginal pain, decides. In the whole model the mean predicted risk is 25% for the 83 women and 54% for the 159 men in the training split. The one-hot inputs for atypical angina, high fasting blood sugar and the abnormal resting-ECG levels are not connected to anything; they are entry nodes of this root without effect, and their information is partly carried by the complementary levels that are connected.

parts.original_hypothesis: The predicted risk is the sigmoid of a sum on the logit scale: the direct linear score, plus the three gates each weighted by its output edge, plus the output bias (formula attached). Two gates raise risk (ST depression; exercise angina in women) and one lowers it (high maximum heart rate). By ablation the direct terms matter most (training AUC 0.947 falls to 0.811 without them), then the ST-depression gate (0.938), the sex and angina gate (0.941) and the heart-rate gate (0.945). Self-probe of the additive combination, on a constructed woman with exercise angina, 2 mm of ST depression, non-anginal pain and a maximum heart rate of 170 bpm: the direct score contributes -8.12, the ST-depression gate 0.62, the sex and angina gate 2.08 and the heart-rate gate -1.26, giving a score of -7.37 and a predicted risk of 0.1%: the gates partly cancel and the direct score, driven by female sex and non-anginal pain, decides. In the whole model the mean predicted risk is 25% for the 83 women and 54% for the 159 men in the training split. The one-hot inputs for atypical angina, high fasting blood sugar and the abnormal resting-ECG levels are not connected to anything; they are entry nodes of this root without effect, and their information is partly carried by the complementary levels that are connected.

parts.original_hypothesis: The direct edges form a linear risk score that carries most of the model's ranking: replacing the whole part by its training mean lowers the training AUC from 0.947 to 0.811. The number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy dominates it, at 2.61 per sd through its own edge (removing that edge alone lowers the AUC to 0.907). Self-probe on the typical case: predicted risk climbs from 12% with no coloured vessels to 71% with one and 98% with two. Female sex lowers the score directly (-1.57 per sd on the female indicator, and 0.39 per sd on the male indicator, which pushes the same way because that indicator is the complement of the female one). A flat ST segment raises it (0.74 per sd) and an upsloping one lowers it (-0.83 per sd); typical angina (-0.78) and non-anginal pain (-0.74 directly, besides its role in the heart-rate gate) lower it relative to the other chest-pain types. Cholesterol raises it (0.87 per sd) and maximum heart rate lowers it (-0.47 per sd directly, besides the heart-rate gate). Normal fasting blood sugar raises the score through its direct edge (0.63 per sd), the opposite of its role inside the ST-depression gate. The remaining edges are listed in the attached formula. parts.name: stDepressionGate
parts.original_hypothesis: Exercise-induced ST depression raises predicted risk through this gate once it passes a threshold; a reversible thallium defect lowers that threshold and a downsloping ST segment pushes it up. Over the training data the gate is open for 116 patients, of whom 66% have heart disease, and for them it adds 1.06 to the model score (logit) on average, through this part. Among the 81 patients with no ST depression it is open for 2; among the 59 with ST depression of 1.5 mm or more and a segment that is not downsloping it is open for every one (share 1.00). Self-probe, sweeping ST depression on the typical case: with a normal thallium scan the gate is still shut at 1 mm (pre-activation -0.25) and open at 1.5 mm (adding 0.21); with a reversible defect it is already open at 0.5 mm (adding 0.27). At 4 mm the whole-model predicted risk is 56% with a normal scan and 89% with a reversible defect (the defect also has its own direct edge). At 2.5 mm a downsloping segment shuts the gate in the typical case (pre-activation -2.84, against a contribution of 1.02 for an upsloping one); downsloping segments are rare, 17 training patients, and the gate is open for 4 of them. Normal fasting blood sugar narrows the gate (at 2.5 mm and upsloping it adds 1.02 with normal sugar and 1.93 with high sugar), but the direct blood-sugar edge pulls the other way, so in the whole model this case's risk falls from 27% to 13% with high sugar.
